card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Former steel fabricator and welder at an offshore support yard. Laid off about fourteen months ago, then signed off with a lower back problem. Now looking, half-heartedly, for something lighter.
card.education_detail: Left a local high school at 16 with a handful of GCSEs at C/D. Did a Level 2 fabrication and welding course at the college in Lowestoft, then an apprenticeship. Holds a couple of welding coding certificates that have since lapsed.
card.household: Lives with his wife Gemma, 33, a senior care assistant who works shifts at a residential home. They rent a two-bed terraced house a short walk from the town centre. There are no children yet. They have a slightly overweight Staffordshire bull terrier called Dexter.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Lowestoft. His dad worked on the trawlers and then the docks, and his mum did school dinners. He was baptised Church of England and married in church. He goes to a carol service at Christmas and the odd funeral, and would tick Christian on a form without thinking twice. It is more family habit than active faith.
card.professional_persona: A capable, practical worker who was good with his hands and fine as long as someone else set the jobs out. He never liked chasing paperwork, renewing tickets or turning up to toolbox talks. Since the layoff and the back trouble his confidence has dipped. He applies for warehouse, forklift and maintenance roles when the Jobcentre nudges him, but often lets applications drift.
card.sports_persona: Follows Ipswich Town, mostly on telly and his phone. He has been to Portman Road a few times with his brother-in-law. He played Sunday league as a teenager and gave it up. These days exercise is walking Dexter along the seafront and doing the stretches the physio gave him, when he remembers.
card.arts_persona: Not into galleries or theatre. He watches a lot of YouTube: restoration videos, welding channels, people rebuilding old motorbikes. He likes long crime dramas he can binge and listens to old indie and Britpop in the car. He once went to see a tribute band at the Marina Theatre because Gemma wanted to.
card.travel_persona: Holidays have mostly been caravan weeks in Norfolk or Cornwall, a stag do in Prague, and a honeymoon in Tenerife. He doesn't mind flying but finds airports stressful and busy. Money is tight now, so the most likely trip is a couple of nights away somewhere in the UK for an anniversary.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the cooking on Gemma's late shifts, but nothing fancy: pasta bakes, chilli, sausage and mash, oven chips. He calls the evening meal dinner. He likes a chippy tea on a Friday from a place near the beach, and a fry-up at weekends. Eats too many crisps in front of the telly.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching restoration and welding videos on YouTube
Tinkering with an old 125cc motorbike in the back yard that he's been 'about to finish' for two years
PlayStation, mostly FIFA and the odd open-world game, usually offline
Walking the dog along the seafront early when it's quiet
Sea fishing off the pier now and then with his brother-in-law
skills: General DIY: shelves, fixing gates, sorting out the car
Cooking simple meals for two on a budget
card.career_goals: Vague. He'd like something steady with regular hours that won't wreck his back, maybe a maintenance or workshop role at a local firm, or getting his forklift licence. He has talked about retraining as a gas engineer, but the cost and the course put him off. Mostly he wants to be bringing money in again so Gemma isn't carrying everything.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly flat Suffolk/East Anglian accent with a slow pace. His answers are short at first and he rarely volunteers more unless asked a follow-up. He says 'er' and 'erm' before most answers, and 'sort of' and 'I dunno' a lot. He says 'yeah' to show he's listening and calls the interviewer 'mate' once he's relaxed. Silence doesn't bother him much. He'll leave a gap rather than fill it, then add a bit more a few seconds later, like 'yeah, it's alright really'. He laughs briefly and drily at himself. He'd say 'knackered' rather than 'tired' and 'skint' about money.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and doesn't bother capitalising 'i' or names. Apostrophes are often missing ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Answers are short, sometimes a single word or 'not really'. He uses commas instead of full stops, or no punctuation at all. Occasional typos he doesn't fix. He uses 'dunno' and 'tbh' now and then and never uses emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit awkward. He's polite and goes along with things but gives very little away at first, and can come across as disinterested when he's really just uncomfortable. He warms up slightly if the conversation turns to something practical he knows about, like welding, bikes or the dog. He won't argue or push back much and tends to say 'yeah, fair enough'.
small_things: Dexter the dog and his dodgy stomach
The weather on the seafront and how windy it gets
The motorbike in the yard he still hasn't finished
Gemma working nights and him having the house to himself
Prices going up at the big Tesco
A welding video he watched where someone rebuilt a rusty trailer
deeper_things: Feeling embarrassed about not working while Gemma does long shifts
Worry that his back won't get properly better and he'll never do heavy work again
Being on benefits and finding the Jobcentre appointments demoralising
He and Gemma have talked about kids but keep putting it off because of money
Feeling a bit low and lacking motivation some days, though he wouldn't call it depression
His dad's health, as he's had a couple of falls this year
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop sits on a low coffee table and he's on the settee leaning forward. Lighting comes mainly from a window to his left, so the left side of his face is brighter and the right is a bit shadowed, with a faint blue tint from the screen. He has a broad, slightly round face, short light-brown hair clippered at the sides and a bit longer on top, and a few days of stubble. No glasses. His expression is neutral to faintly uneasy, with his mouth closed and eyes looking just below the camera at the screen. He wears a plain navy hoodie with the cuffs pushed up. Behind him is a grey fabric settee back with a rumpled fleece throw, and a magnolia wall with a framed wedding photo slightly off-centre. A shelf holds a PlayStation controller, a small Ipswich Town mug and a stack of post. The edge of a radiator with a towel drying on it is visible at the right of the frame.
